key_insight: Nanoindentation can trigger localized amorphous-to-bcc devitrification in amorphous refractory metals, and their crystal forming ability varies strongly across the series, decreasing roughly from V to W.
engineering_relevance: This suggests refractory amorphous coatings may differ substantially in contact-induced crystallization resistance, which matters for wear, durability, and mechanical reliability in harsh environments.
method: Melt-quenched amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W were prepared at 300 K.
Interatomic potentials were validated against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions.
Large-scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation was used to track bcc nucleation, growth, and coalescence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a sigmoidal bcc-fraction-versus-depth response, a CFA spanning about a factor of four, and a velocity scaling of CFA ∝ v^-m with mean exponent 1.08.
watch_item: Results are based on molecular dynamics and potential models, so quantitative trends may depend on the chosen interatomic potentials and idealized indentation conditions.
paper_title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
